summary: Part one of the City Sample procedural-city guide: set up the CitySample Houdini source files, then use the City Layout, City Zone, Freeway Util Curve Attribute, City Processor and City_Lot_Processor operators in Houdini to lay out roads, zones and a freeway and export PBC data for import into UE.
gotchas: Requires a SideFX Houdini install; version 18.5.532 recommended
Workflow only tested on Windows 10
Needs 2 GB free disk for small cities, 5-10 GB for bigger ones
City Processor cooking can take several minutes; switch Houdini to Manual mode while wiring inputs

summary: Shows how to batch-generate Static Mesh LODs from editor Blueprints or Python with EditorStaticMeshLibrary (set_lods with reduction settings, LOD Group assignment, removing LODs) and how to copy a LOD from another Static Mesh with set_lod_from_static_mesh, then save the asset.
gotchas: Requires the Editor Scripting Utilities plugin
The first EditorScriptingMeshReductionSettings entry has no effect; LOD 0 always keeps all triangles
LOD changes modify the asset and must be saved explicitly with Save Asset / save_loaded_asset
set_lod_from_static_mesh cannot replace LOD 0 (index must be > 0) and copies the LOD with no ongoing link to the source

summary: Explains the PCG tools and custom nodes in the Electric Dreams sample: the Level to PCG Asset Utility that exports a level's meshes into a PCG Settings point cloud, the Actor Tagger widget, hierarchy-preserving copy (SG_CopyPointsWithHierarchy/ApplyHierarchy), the Flat Area Detector subgraph (DiscardPointsInBumpyAreas) and the LookAt node.
gotchas: Level to PCG utility needs Show Plugin Content enabled to find it
World Partition / OFPA levels must be opened and loaded in the editor before export
In hierarchies, transform the RelativeTransform attribute (Apply To Attribute), not the point Transform
Custom nodes other than the Level to PCG utility live in the Electric Dreams sample content, not the engine

summary: Guide to the Broadcast Hype Chamber esports motion-graphics sample: playing graphics via BP_HypeChamber_Controller, Remote Control preset and web app, data-table-driven team themes, adding teams, and batch rendering with Movie Render Queue through an Editor Utility Widget.
gotchas: Disable Use Mode Select before rendering with Movie Render Queue
Remote Control web app runs on port 7000

summary: Overview of the City Sample (Matrix Awakens) project: system specs, maps and controls, and how it uses Lumen with Hardware Ray Tracing, Nanite, TSR, Virtual Shadow Maps, local exposure, World Partition/OFPA/Data Layers, Mass AI (MassEntity, ZoneGraph, StateTree, Smart Objects), Chaos Vehicles with Control Rig deformation, and MetaSounds/Soundscape audio.
gotchas: Requires DirectX 12; recommends 64 GB RAM, RTX 2080 and at least 8 GB VRAM, installed on an SSD
Big City cells are unloaded by default and must be loaded via the World Partition window
With Nanite meshes, Hardware Ray Tracing only traces the Nanite fallback mesh
Mass AI features are described as experimental

summary: Setup and navigation guide for the Electric Dreams Environment sample (PCG, Substrate, Lumen, Nanite, Soundscape): system specs, the list of full and breakdown PCG levels with content paths, drone controls and sequence shortcuts.
gotchas: Requires DirectX 12; minimum spec RTX 2080 with 8 GB VRAM and 32 GB RAM
Main levels are resource-intensive 4 km x 4 km World Partition maps with streaming disabled
On minimum spec, use 1080p at 50% screen percentage

summary: Reference for the Automotive Materials Pack on Fab: 10 PBR master materials (Additive, Brake Rotor, Car Paint, Decal, Emissive, Glass, Masked, Opaque, Textile, Tint) with triplanar mapping by default and ray-tracing-optimized branches, plus their exposed parameters.
gotchas: Vehicle meshes shown are not included in the pack
Triplanar mapping uses local space, so results depend on mesh orientation relative to its pivot

summary: How to enable and use the Quixel Bridge plugin to browse, download and add Megascans assets and MetaHumans to a project, including download resolutions (Nanite tier), library path, export settings and drag-and-drop placement.
gotchas: Marked Deprecated; Megascans content is now available through Fab
Requires an internet connection and an Epic account on the Unreal Unlimited plan
Atlases, Displacements and Brushes are not supported
Export Settings must be configured before adding an asset to the scene

summary: Breakdown of the Stack O Bot third-person platformer sample (UE 5.6): where to find its character Blueprint with Control Rig, PCG-built level and fence/coin splines, vertex-color UV-less materials, HLODs, StateTree NPCs, level instances, physics grab/destruction, custom camera manager and objective/portal system.
gotchas: Current sample is built for engine version 5.6; older versions need the older download
Objects tagged Main World Only appear only when a level instance is played standalone

summary: Describes the Content Examples project from Fab and lists each of its example maps (animation, retargeting, Blueprint communication/input, Chaos destruction, CommonUI, IK Rig, landscapes, materials, NavMesh, Niagara, physics, post processing, UMG, volumes and more).
gotchas: Cascade maps use the deprecated Cascade system; use the Niagara maps instead
Niagara_Fluids simulations must run in PIE

summary: Hub page: links to feature showcase samples Electric Dreams, City Sample, Broadcast Hype Chamber, In-Camera VFX Production Test, Meerkat Demo, Pixel Streaming sample, Slay and Virtual Studio.
Hub page for free Epic content on Fab (filter Price > Free): links to Quixel Bridge, the Automotive Materials Pack guide, and Live Link and Professional Video I/O plugin pages.
Hub page: links to the Lyra, Valley of the Ancient and Stack O Bot sample game breakdowns.

How to use the Modeling Mode Paint Vertex Colors tool to paint per-asset RGBA vertex colors (including on Nanite meshes): brush actions, secondary brushes, channel filters, quick actions like fill/copy channel/copy to LODs, and hotkeys; contrasts it with per-instance Mesh Paint Mode.
gotchas: Beta feature
Paints asset vertex colors only; all instances share them (use Mesh Paint Mode for per-instance)
Per-instance vertex colors are not supported on Nanite meshes
Viewport Vertex Colors visualization does not work on Nanite meshes

summary: Hub page explaining how to get Epic sample projects through Fab (website, Launcher Fab Library, or the in-editor Fab plugin via Window > Fab) and linking to templates, feature examples, Content Examples, sample games and free content.
gotchas: Sample projects only appear in Fab Library when a compatible engine version is installed
Fab plugin is for 5.3+; on 5.3/5.4 it must be downloaded separately

summary: Short hub page defining Assets as the content building blocks of a project (meshes, materials, Blueprints, sounds) and advising they be managed through the Content Browser; child links not listed.
gotchas: Always manage assets through the Content Browser

summary: Explains Data-Only Blueprints: Blueprint classes that only override inherited defaults, edited in a compact property editor and converted to full Blueprints once code, variables or components are added.
gotchas: No new elements can be added in data-only mode; adding code, variables or components converts it to a full Blueprint

summary: Lists the ways to create Blueprint class assets: Content Browser Add New / Asset View / Asset Tree with a parent class, Level Editor Convert Selection to Blueprint Class (New Subclass, Child Actors, Harvest Components), and Create Blueprint from the Class Viewer.
gotchas: New Subclass is only available with a single Actor selected
Harvest Components suits mesh-container actors, not AI characters that need per-actor autonomy

summary: Steps to host platform SDKs for Turnkey on a Google Drive shared drive: create a Google Cloud app with Drive API and OAuth credentials, place client_id.json and reference it in TurnkeyManifest.xml, lay out the SdkInstallers folders, and write FileSource entries.
gotchas: First connection opens a browser for authentication and Turnkey waits until it completes
Zip SDKs before uploading; Drive downloads of single files are much faster

summary: Reference for writing Turnkey manifest XML to distribute platform SDKs: TurnkeyManifest/TurnkeyStudioSettings files, AdditionalManifests chaining, FileSource fields (Platform, Type Full/AutoSDK/Flash, Version, Name, Source), copy providers (file:, perforce:, googledrive:), fileexpansion/listexpansion and built-in variables.
gotchas: Platform names must match engine names (Win64, not Windows)
fileexpansion: must be followed by a copy provider prefix
Turnkey prefers AutoSDK over Full when both exist
macOS needs an extra smb: prefix for SMB shares

summary: Reference for the editor toolbar Platforms dropdown: install/manage SDKs via Turnkey, Package Project for a platform with build target/configuration options, Packaging Settings, Device Manager, Quick Launch and the Project Launcher with custom launch profiles.
gotchas: Installing SDKs through the menu requires a TurnkeyManifest pointing to an SDK file repository
Only devices claimed in Device Manager appear in the Project Launcher

summary: Reference for running Turnkey via RunUAT.bat turnkey: interactive menu and -command= arguments for InstallSdk, VerifySdk, ExecuteBuild (cook and package a project), InstallBuild, ListPlatforms, ListSdks, ManageSettings, Control and Test.
gotchas: InstallBuild is described as work in progress
Use engine platform names such as -Platform=Win64, not Windows
Entering 0 cancels the current menu

summary: Brief page noting Diversion is a cloud version control system usable with UE via its plugin, desktop app or CLI, and pointing to Diversion's own docs.
Stub page: Lore is an open-source version control system maintained by Epic; points to Lore.org and UEFN collaboration docs.

Describes Anchorpoint, a Git-based version control app with file locking and Git LFS management, and its Fab plugin that talks to the desktop app so you can lock, commit, diff Blueprints, pull and revert from inside the Unreal Editor.
gotchas: Needs both the Fab plugin and the Anchorpoint desktop application (plugin communicates over IPC)

summary: How to set up a Perforce server (P4D/P4S), configure the P4 typemap and .p4ignore, create a workspace, add the right project folders via P4V, and connect from the editor's Source Control login.
gotchas: Use a case-insensitive Perforce server to avoid issues with tools like UnrealGameSync
Initial file add must be done outside the editor via P4V
Cloud-hosted servers may need Host and Password set in the advanced login fields

summary: How to set up Subversion with VisualSVN and TortoiseSVN, create a working copy, add and commit project folders, connect from the editor's Source Control dialog, and fix HTTPS keychain errors on macOS.
gotchas: Working copy checkout cannot be done inside the editor
HTTPS certificate must be issued to the exact hostname or IP users connect with
macOS may need a one-time svn info login to store the password in the keychain

summary: Syntax reference for Horde agent-selection condition strings: dynamically typed values, size suffixes, and boolean, integer and string operators including case-insensitive regex match.
gotchas: String comparison and regex matching are case-insensitive
A condition is true if any value of a multi-valued key satisfies it

summary: Overview of Horde's editor telemetry collection: telemetry stores selected via APIEndpointET in DefaultEngine.ini, metric aggregation and dashboard charts configured in globals.json, and telemetry sinks in Server.json.

Overview of Horde CI: running BuildGraph scripts on agents, enabling CI via Globals.json, .project.json and .stream.json, agent types, job templates with Text/List/MultiList/TagPicker/Bool parameters, schedules, workspaces and AutoSDK configuration.
gotchas: Built around Perforce workspaces synced on agents

summary: Orientation to Horde configuration: Server.json vs Globals.json, ConfigPath, live reload, project/stream config files, reading configs from Perforce, and using the Horde JSON schema server in Visual Studio.
gotchas: Projects and streams must be configured to use CI, PerfMem Hub and Test Hub
